qs.q: Which acinar zone receives the highest concentration of oxygenated blood?
qs.e: Zone 1 (periportal) is closest to the hepatic artery and portal vein branches, receiving the best oxygenation.
qs.s: Weekly Liver Histology and Physiology Exam - March 7, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Acinar zones are numbered 1 through 3 based on:
o: Order of blood contact and oxygenation
qs.e: Zones are numbered based on the sequence in which blood flows through them from the portal triad (1) to the central vein (3).
qs.s: Weekly Liver Histology and Physiology Exam - March 7, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

es.q: Describe the differences in oxygenation and susceptibility to injury between Acinar Zone 1 and Acinar Zone 3 of the liver. Provide one specific cause of injury for each zone.
es.m: Acinar Zone 1 (periportal) has the best oxygenation, while Acinar Zone 3 (centrilobular) has the worst oxygenation (2 marks). Zone 1 is affected by toxins such as phosphorus poisoning or conditions like eclampsia. (1 mark) Zone 3 is susceptible to injury from alcohol, CCl4, ischemia, shock, and right heart failure. (2 marks)
es.s: Liver Histology, Physiology and Pathology — Practice Questions

es.q: A patient presents with acute liver injury following exposure to carbon tetrachloride. Which acinar zone would be predominantly affected, and what other conditions or toxins are associated with injury to this specific zone?
es.m: Zone 3 (Centrilobular) would be predominantly affected. Other conditions/toxins associated with injury to this zone include alcohol, ischemia, shock, and right heart failure.
es.s: Liver Histology, Physiology and Pathology — Practice Questions

es.q: Identify the main structural and functional units of the liver. Describe the acinar zone most susceptible to hypoxic injury, listing specific pathologies associated with injury to this zone.
es.m: The main structural unit of the liver is the lobule, and the functional unit is the acinus. The acinar zone most susceptible to hypoxic injury is Zone 3 (Centrilobular zone), which has the worst oxygenation. Specific pathologies associated with injury to this zone include alcohol abuse, CCl4 toxicity, ischemia, shock, and right heart failure.
es.s: Liver Histology, Physiology and Pathology — Practice Questions

es.q: A patient presents with acute liver injury secondary to severe right heart failure. Which acinar zone would you expect to be most affected and why?
es.m: Zone 3 (centrilobular) would be most affected. This zone has the worst oxygenation, making it highly susceptible to ischemic injury, as seen in conditions like right heart failure.
es.s: Liver Histology, Physiology and Pathology — Practice Questions
